As creativity blooms and new applications are developed, the players can unlock additional options and modules, learn more about basic business and strategic ideas as well as various programming languages including Python, JavaScript, C++ and many others. Basically, I either feel like I'm not playing well enough if I don't speed up studying, or I feel thoroughly bored if I go ahead and do it, because it just takes forever to find every person who improves their skill and do the speedup procedure 2 or 3 times. Once I get a hardware team and have to train them up, I usually can't take it anymore and quit. Hiring people is also quite tedious. [...] GameBiz 1

  
Then I played another game similar to that and its name was GameBiz. I started playing from the first Edition GameBiz 1 and it as a lot more fun as the Android game. It had a lot more depth feeling for me and most importantly you had a Competition, Publishers and so on.. But the GUI was more or less text based. I would give it a 6 out of 10.  
  

GameBiz 2

  
Then I tried GameBiz 2 which hsa still a similar GUI like GameBiz 1 but has a better feel to it. I would give it a 7 out of 10. Like the first GameBiz it had competition, and you could also sell your engines or license them.  
  

Game Dev Tycoon [...] #3

 .  
  
I generally agree with your assessment of the different games, but I'd give Gamebiz 1 and 2 a bit higher scores. Gamebiz 3 probably is the best game development simulator thus far indeed, with only Mad Games Tycoon as competition. However, I have a very hard time enjoying GB3 due to the extremely tedious training system. Basically, I either feel like I'm not playing well enough if I don't speed up studying, or I feel thoroughly bored if I go ahead and do it, because it just takes forever to find every person who improves their skill and do the speedup procedure 2 or 3 times. Once I get a hardware team and have to train them up, I usually can't take it anymore and quit. Hiring people is also quite tedious.
